question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

I am looking forward to meet you at the conference tomorrow.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of the phrase "**to meet you**".
 
• The correct phrase should be "**to meeting you**", as **"looking forward to"** is followed by a** gerund (verb+ing).**
 
• Thus, the error is located in **Option 3** of the sentence

**Correct Sentence:** *"I am looking forward **to meeting you** at the conference tomorrow."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "No error"** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in Option 3.
 
• **Option 2: "at the conference tomorrow."** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 4: "I am looking forward,"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any change.
